facts.fact: Irène, aged sixty-nine and alone, lived hidden and discreetly in a small flat at 75 rue de la Tour, in the same chic 16th arrondissement she had always known.
facts.quote: Irène was living discreetly in the same arrondissement—in a small flat at 75 rue de la Tour. Alone at age sixty-nine.

facts.fact: Per her granddaughter Lorraine, Irène survived by hiding under her late second husband's Italian surname Sampieri, so no one in her building suspected she was a Jew.
facts.quote: She believed that Irène saved her life by using her late second husband’s Italian last name, Sampieri.

facts.fact: For help she did not turn to high-level ministers the way her son-in-law did; she used a dodgy political fixer, Georges Prade (nicknamed 'Yo Yo'), who knew which doors to knock on.
facts.quote: She did not turn for formal help to high-level ministers, the way her son-in-law did, with his connections and his stiff, formal letters. She had a dodgy political fixer named Georges Prade who knew the doors to knock on.

facts.fact: In September 1941 Prade wrote to Xavier Vallat asking that the annual pension be allowed to flow from daughter Béatrice to Irène; within about a week Vallat's financial section found a loophole and approved it, labelling the payment a repayment of an old debt.
facts.quote: To circumvent that system, in September 1941 Prade intervened, writing a letter to Xavier Vallat asking him to allow the pension to flow from Béatrice to her mother.

facts.fact: Irène was granted an 'Aryan' certificate declaring her 'Ne doit pas être regardé comme juif' — a fiction everyone knew, since all four of her grandparents were Jewish and her mother Louise had never converted.
facts.quote: The certificate said it plainly: “Ne doit pas être regardé comme juif”—“Must not be considered a Jew.” It was a fiction, and everyone knew it. All four of her grandparents were Jewish.

facts.fact: In the early hours of October 3 seven synagogues were bombed with dynamite (six damaged), including rue de la Victoire where Irène had married and mourned her son; the shift from legal exclusion to open terror, executed by French agents under Gestapo chief Helmut Knochen.
facts.quote: In the hours between one and five in the morning on October 3, seven synagogues were targeted with bombs. Dynamite was planted at the doorways, and six of the synagogues were damaged.

facts.fact: Irène's younger brother Charles was conned by the pseudo-attaché forger André Barrié, who sold him a fake 'honorary Aryan' certificate — they settled the price at 3 million francs — and Charles learned at Vichy's Service des informations that the signature was fake.
facts.quote: They dickered over the price of 10 million francs and settled on 3 million francs, worth roughly $1.3 million today.

facts.fact: After the con Charles fled to the free zone with his son-in-law Armand de Dampierre, buying a modest château in the Gers in June 1941 and turning it into a Resistance safehouse with a British B2 radio transmitter.
facts.quote: Charles didn’t pause. He managed to flee to the free zone with his son-in-law, Count Armand de Dampierre, and bought a modest château in Gers in June 1941.
